main_text.p: Quemadmodum non incommodè illi ma-nus baptizandi, baptizabat tamen, sic & Hebraeis ex abundanti charitate scribit. Summopere sanè de illis sollicitus, pro quibus & anathema fieri exoptavit. Subjungit tempus exaratæ Epistolæ, facitq; salvo vetustiorem posteriori ad Timotheum.

XXXIV. Tandem subnectimus Græcorum Codicum, plerorumque & antiquissimorum fidem. Quorum constans inscriptio est, τὰ ἁγίας πύλας [?], vel πρὸς τὰς [illegible, ~6 letters] Ἀποστόλας, ἡ πρὸς Ἑβραίους Ἐπιστολή. Beza sub initium annotationum, Ita scriptum invenimus in omnibus nostris Codicibus, uno tantum excepto, in quo duntaxat scriptum erat, πρὸς Ἑβραίους. Idem codices R. Stephano in recensione suâ N. T. usurpati. Cujus quanquam inscriptionis originem non ab ipso Paulo derivemus, & antiqua fuerit, & Græcorum in eo consensus argumentum. Syrus simpliciter, אגרת [?] עברית [?] Epistola ad Hebraeos. Sed inscriptionis illa ratio communis aliis Epistolis, quoad Syrum Interpretem, neque Pauli nomen hic tacitum magis quam

page.notes: Page is heavily damaged by ink spread and speckling, so many letters are doubtful. The Greek and Hebrew lines in the middle and the Hebrew title are only partly legible and are marked [?]. The page number and the first word of the running head are partly obscured. The first line of the page is blurred; its words are marked as read but are uncertain. The line "XXXIV." opens a numbered paragraph, so it is kept as running text and not made a heading.
